purpose: Define Digest -- monokl's content-identity type -- per docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md §8.4, which supersedes the bare-hex ContentHash(String) of docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 12. A Digest names its algorithm, so a cache entry written today stays distinguishable from one written after an algorithm or width change. FileAnalysis (track #14), the in-memory cache (track #16) and disk persistence (track #17) key on it.
scope: The Digest struct and DigestAlgorithm enum in crates/monokl/src/digest.rs; Digest::blake3(content) as the one hashing constructor; the textual form `algorithm ":" encoded` produced by Display and accepted by FromStr; the serde wire form, which is that same string; and the parse errors.
non_goals: Computing sha256 digests. DigestAlgorithm::Sha256 exists so a sha256 digest from a third-party harness plugin parses and round-trips (§8.4's boundary table); monokl computes blake3 only, and nothing in monokl needs a sha256 hasher yet.
sha512 or any other OCI-registered algorithm. DigestAlgorithm is #[non_exhaustive] so one can be added without a breaking change.
Moving Digest into wisp-contracts. That crate does not exist yet; Digest is shaped to move there unchanged (docs/adr/0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md).
FileAnalysis, the cache, and the cache.json format (tracks #14, #16, #17). They reference Digest; their own shapes are not locked here.
The cache Tier-1 mtime/size fast-path gap (docs/architecture/cache-architecture.md). It concerns when a digest is compared, not the digest's shape.
Streaming or incremental hashing. Digest::blake3 hashes one byte slice in one call.

api_surface.name: DigestAlgorithm
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)] #[non_exhaustive] pub enum DigestAlgorithm { Sha256, Blake3 }
api_surface.description: The algorithm half of a digest. Its textual names are `sha256` and `blake3`.

api_surface.name: Digest
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)] pub struct Digest { pub algorithm: DigestAlgorithm, pub bytes: [u8; 32] }

api_surface.name: impl FromStr for Digest
api_surface.signature: impl std::str::FromStr for Digest { type Err = DigestParseError; }
api_surface.description: Parses `algorithm:hex`. Rejects an unknown algorithm, a missing separator, hex of the wrong length, and any character outside [0-9a-f], uppercase hex included.

api_surface.name: DigestParseError
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)] #[non_exhaustive] pub enum DigestParseError { MissingSeparator, UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: String }, InvalidEncoding }
api_surface.description: Why a string is not a digest.

api_surface.name: Serialize / Deserialize for Digest
api_surface.signature: impl Serialize for Digest; impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Digest
api_surface.description: Serializes as the Display string; deserializes from a string through FromStr, so an invalid digest fails to deserialize.
error_conditions: any FromStr error, surfaced as a serde custom error

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Digest::blake3(b"") equals Digest { algorithm: DigestAlgorithm::Blake3, bytes: *blake3::hash(b"").as_bytes() }, and its Display output is exactly "blake3:af1349b9f5f9a1a6a0404dea36dcc9499bcb25c9adc112b7cc9a93cae41f3262" (blake3's published digest of empty input).
Digest::blake3 is deterministic: two calls on byte-identical input return equal values, and calls on different inputs b"a" and b"b" return unequal values.
For every digest d, d.to_string().parse::<Digest>() returns Ok(d), for both DigestAlgorithm::Blake3 and DigestAlgorithm::Sha256 and for bytes of all zeros, all 0xff, and a blake3 output.
Display writes the algorithm name (`blake3` or `sha256`), one `:`, then exactly 64 characters from [0-9a-f]; no uppercase letter ever appears.
Parsing a string with no `:` (e.g. a bare 64-character hex string, the old ContentHash form) returns Err(DigestParseError::MissingSeparator).

Parsing `md5:` followed by 64 valid hex characters returns Err(DigestParseError::UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: "md5" }). Algorithm names are case-sensitive: `BLAKE3:` followed by valid hex also returns UnknownAlgorithm.

Parsing `blake3:` followed by any of these returns Err(DigestParseError::InvalidEncoding): 63 hex characters, 65 hex characters, an empty string, 64 characters containing one uppercase hex letter (OCI: [A-F] MUST NOT be used), and 64 characters containing a non-hex character such as `g`. A second `:` in the encoded part (`blake3:ab:cd...`) is also InvalidEncoding.
serde_json::to_string(&d) is the JSON string literal of d.to_string() (e.g. "\"blake3:af13...\""), and serde_json::from_str::<Digest> of that literal returns d.
serde_json::from_str::<Digest> fails (returns Err, never panics) for a JSON string that FromStr rejects (each AC-005..AC-007 case), and for null, a number, a boolean, an array, and an object.
Digest and DigestAlgorithm are Copy and usable as HashMap/HashSet keys; equal digests hash equally. Neither implements PartialOrd/Ord or Default.

linked_research: docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md §8.4 and §14; OCI image-spec descriptor digest grammar; docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 12 (superseded).
revision_note: 2026-10-23 correction: replaced ContentHash(String) with Digest per Part 8 §8.4, which supersedes it (§14). An unprefixed hash is unmigratable, and the old spec explicitly declined deserialize-time validation; Digest validates on parse and deserialize. The earlier ContentHash criteria are withdrawn, not carried over.
reasoning: Shape, grammar and the lowercase rule come straight from §8.4. Choices this spec makes that §8.4 leaves open: a single blake3 constructor (sha256 is parse-only, non_goals); DigestAlgorithm is #[non_exhaustive] because OCI registers more algorithms; serde goes through the Display/FromStr string so the wire form and the text form cannot drift; a second `:` is InvalidEncoding rather than a separate variant, since the encoded part is what is malformed. Digest lives in monokl until wisp-contracts exists (ADR 0002).
